descriptions.after:
A dictionary that supports the following options:
  • Temporary — Boolean. Whether to open the script in a preview tab. Default is false.
  • HighlightRange — A nested dictionary containing a line and character range to highlight in the editor. Example: HighlightRange = { Start = { Line = 10, Character = 1 }, End = { Line = 15, Character = 20 }}. Lines and characters are 1-based. Out-of-range positions are clamped to the nearest valid position: a Line or Character below 1 becomes 1, a Character past the end of its line becomes the end of that line, and a Line past the last line becomes the end of the script. Start and End are clamped independently; if End is before Start after clamping, they are swapped, so the same text is highlighted with the cursor at the later position.
  • InitialReadOnlyReasons — An array of strings. Reasons to add with ScriptDocument:AddReadOnlyReasonsAsync() once the editor opens, so the script is read-only as soon as the call returns. Example: InitialReadOnlyReasons = { "MyPluginTemplateScript" }.

descriptions.before: Determines whether hit detection and spatial queries use the individual body parts or the single collider when CollisionMode is AvatarSettingsCollisionMode.SingleCollider.
descriptions.after: Determines whether hit detection and spatial queries use the individual body parts, the single collider, or a separate hitbox when CollisionMode is AvatarSettingsCollisionMode.SingleCollider.

descriptions.before: Individual avatar body parts handle Touched events and spatial queries (CanTouch and CanQuery enabled on body parts) while the single collider part has CanTouch and CanQuery disabled. This is the default value for HitAndTouchDetectionMode.
descriptions.after:
Deprecated:
Individual avatar body parts handle Touched events and spatial queries (CanTouch and CanQuery enabled on body parts) while the single collider part has CanTouch and CanQuery disabled. This is the default value for HitAndTouchDetectionMode.

descriptions.before: The single collider part handles Touched events and spatial queries (CanTouch and CanQuery enabled on the collider) while all individual body parts have CanTouch and CanQuery disabled.
descriptions.after:
Deprecated:
The single collider part handles Touched events and spatial queries (CanTouch and CanQuery enabled on the collider) while all individual body parts have CanTouch and CanQuery disabled.

Deprecated:
A separate, noncolliding, massless hitbox part sized by HitboxSize handles Touched events and spatial queries (CanTouch and CanQuery enabled on the hitbox) while the single collider and all individual body parts have CanTouch and CanQuery disabled. Like the collider, the hitbox hangs from the top of the body and rests on the floor when it is taller than the body, so it can reach the floor without changing what the character stands on or steps over. The hitbox is removed when the character dies.

descriptions.before: Creates six invisible box collider parts welded to R15 limbs to approximate classic R6 collision geometry. The engine spawns six invisible Part instances (head, torso, left arm, right arm, left leg, right leg) parented to the character and welded to the corresponding R15 body parts. All original R15 mesh parts have their BasePart.CanCollide, BasePart.CanTouch, and BasePart.CanQuery disabled and are made massless; only the HumanoidRootPart retains mass so it remains the physics assembly root.
descriptions.after:
Deprecated:
Creates six invisible box collider parts welded to R15 limbs to approximate classic R6 collision geometry. The engine spawns six invisible Part instances (head, torso, left arm, right arm, left leg, right leg) parented to the character and welded to the corresponding R15 body parts. All original R15 mesh parts have their BasePart.CanCollide, BasePart.CanTouch, and BasePart.CanQuery disabled and are made massless; only the HumanoidRootPart retains mass so it remains the physics assembly root.

descriptions.before: Overrides each R15 mesh part's collision physics with inner-box geometry derived from the standard R15 scaling model. The engine recalculates every MeshPart in the character with collision data from the default R15 model's bounding dimensions, producing tighter collision volumes that follow the avatar's proportions without adding extra parts. This is the default value of LegacyCollisionMode.
descriptions.after:

Overrides each R15 mesh part's collision physics with inner-box geometry derived from the standard R15 scaling model. The engine recalculates every MeshPart in the character with collision data from the default R15 model's bounding dimensions, producing tighter collision volumes that follow the avatar's proportions without adding extra parts. This is the default value of LegacyCollisionMode.
Determines whether touch detection and spatial queries use the individual body parts, the single collider, or a separate hitbox when CollisionMode is AvatarSettingsCollisionMode.SingleCollider.

Individual avatar body parts handle Touched events and spatial queries (CanTouch and CanQuery enabled on body parts) while the single collider part has CanTouch and CanQuery disabled. This is the default value for TouchAndQueryDetectionMode.
The single collider part handles Touched events and spatial queries (CanTouch and CanQuery enabled on the collider) while all individual body parts have CanTouch and CanQuery disabled.

A separate, noncolliding, massless hitbox part sized by HitboxSize handles Touched events and spatial queries (CanTouch and CanQuery enabled on the hitbox) while the single collider and all individual body parts have CanTouch and CanQuery disabled. Like the collider, the hitbox hangs from the top of the body and rests on the floor when it is taller than the body, so it can reach the floor without changing what the character stands on or steps over. The hitbox is removed when the character dies.

Deprecated: Workspace.AvatarUnificationMode no longer has an effect; R6 avatars always load as R6 rigs.
Disables the R6-to-R15 adapter; R6 avatars in an R6 experience load using the standard R6 rig with no adapter parts applied.

descriptions.before: Enables the R6-to-R15 adapter; R6 avatars joining an R6 experience receive invisible R15 adapter MeshParts welded to their R6-named joints, preserving R6 scale while enabling R15 features such as layered clothing and animatable heads.
descriptions.after:
Deprecated: Workspace.AvatarUnificationMode no longer has an effect; R6 avatars always load as R6 rigs.
Enables the R6-to-R15 adapter; R6 avatars joining an R6 experience receive invisible R15 adapter MeshParts welded to their R6-named joints, preserving R6 scale while enabling R15 features such as layered clothing and animatable heads.

descriptions.before: A non-nil Opaque reference contained in Content.Opaque.
descriptions.after: Opaque content whose underlying data isn't accessible from scripts. Both Content.Uri and Content.Object are nil.
Indicates that the associated User ID is scoped to a specific experience. The domain ID corresponds to the universe ID of that experience.

Indicates that the associated User ID is scoped to a specific group (community). The domain ID corresponds to the group ID. This item is not yet supported: User values with this domain type can't be created.
The user ID is scoped to a specific OAuth application. The domain ID is the application ID.

descriptions.before: The camera holds its vertical field of view constant when the viewport is resized.
descriptions.after: The camera holds its vertical field of view constant when the viewport is resized. The ViewStretch will apply to the horizontal axis.

descriptions.before: The camera holds its diagonal field of view constant when the viewport is resized.
descriptions.after: The camera holds its diagonal field of view constant when the viewport is resized. The ViewStretch will apply to the horizontal axis.

descriptions.before: The camera holds the field of view along the longer viewport axis constant when the viewport is resized.
descriptions.after: The camera holds the field of view along the longer viewport axis constant when the viewport is resized. The ViewStretch will apply to the horizontal axis.

The color/transparency sequence radiates outward from the element's center in an ellipse, optionally shifted by Offset. The ellipse's horizontal and vertical radii are half the element's width and height, respectively, so the ellipse fits the element's bounds. Rotation rotates the ellipse's axes.
The possible ways in which the gui navigation can be moved.
No direction. Used when no direction applies to the selection changing (e.g. if modified by a script).
The up direction (negative Y in the viewport) in directional navigation.
The down direction (positive Y in the viewport) in directional navigation.
The down direction (negative X in the viewport) in directional navigation.
The right direction (positive X in the viewport) in directional navigation.
The forward direction in sequential navigation.
The backward direction in sequential navigation.

descriptions.before: The scroll delta (change) of a mouse wheel. Primarily used in the Input Action System.
descriptions.after: The scroll delta (change) of a mouse wheel. Primarily used in the Input Action System, returning a velocity in scroll units per second (where one scroll unit is approximately equivalent to a standard mouse wheel notch) under a Direction1D action type.

descriptions.before: The pan delta (change) from a trackpad two-finger pan gesture. Primarily used in the Input Action System.
descriptions.after: The pan delta (change) from a trackpad two-finger pan gesture. Primarily used in the Input Action System, returning a velocity in pixels per second under a Direction2D action type.

descriptions.before: The scale delta (change) from a trackpad two-finger pinch gesture. Primarily used in the Input Action System.
descriptions.after: The scale delta (change) from a trackpad two-finger pinch gesture. Primarily used in the Input Action System, returning a velocity in scroll units per second (where one scroll unit is approximately equivalent to a standard mouse wheel notch) under a Direction1D action type.

descriptions.before: The movement delta (change) of the mouse cursor. Primarily used in the Input Action System.
descriptions.after: The movement delta (change) of the mouse cursor. Primarily used in the Input Action System, returning a velocity in pixels per second under a Direction2D action type.

descriptions.before: The movement delta (change) of a touch input. Primarily used in the Input Action System.
descriptions.after: The movement delta (change) of a touch input. Primarily used in the Input Action System, returning a velocity in pixels per second under a Direction2D action type.

descriptions.before: The scale delta (change) of a two-finger touch pinch gesture. Primarily used in the Input Action System.
descriptions.after: The scale delta (change) from a touch two-finger pinch gesture. Primarily used in the Input Action System, returning a velocity in pixels per second under a Direction1D action type.
Sets which screen axis OrthographicSize is applied to.
The screen's vertical axis will span exactly OrthographicSize studs. The ViewStretch will apply to the horizontal axis.
The screen's horizontal axis will span exactly OrthographicSize studs. The ViewStretch will apply to the vertical axis.
The screen diagonal will span exactly OrthographicSize studs. The ViewStretch will apply to the horizontal axis. (In the initial beta, a bug makes it apply to both axes in a complex way.)
The screen's longer axis will span exactly OrthographicSize studs. The ViewStretch will apply to the shorter axis. If both dimensions are identical, it will apply to the horizontal axis.
The decision that IntegrityService.EvaluatePlayerDeviceTrust returns for a player.
The player stays in the server.
The player is disconnected from the server and sees a rejection message.
The trust level of a player's device.
Roblox is still checking the device. Every player starts at this level, and some players might stay at it for the whole session.
Roblox can't tell whether the device is trusted, because the player is on an unsupported platform or an error occurred on the Roblox side. The device might or might not be trustworthy.
The device failed the check, or the player is on a platform that can't be verified.
The device passed some of the checks, but not all of them.
The device passed every check.
Chooses between perspective and orthographic cameras.
The camera is perspective, and uses the field of view settings.
The camera is orthographic, and uses the orthographic settings.
Result codes returned by AvatarCreationService:PromptCreateMakeupAsync() that describe the overall makeup look creation outcome.
All submitted makeup assets and the makeup look were created successfully.
At least one makeup asset was created, but one or more assets or the final makeup look composition did not succeed.
No makeup assets could be created, so the makeup look was not created.
The player declined the makeup creation prompt.
The makeup creation prompt timed out before the player responded.
The player did not respond to the makeup creation prompt.
An unexpected or unclassified error prevented makeup look creation.
The makeup assets or creation tokens failed validation before upload.

descriptions.after: Teleport was initiated by TeleportService:TeleportToPrivateServer(), a deprecated method that sends players to a reserved server using a legacy access code.
